R129.note: Adds passwordEncoder.matches() verification plus a dummy-hash timing-safe path on user-not-found/null credentials; PasswordEncoder dependency is required for the fix, not an unrelated restriction.

R130.note: JexlSandbox is left permissive-by-default with only 5 classes blacklisted (Runtime/ProcessBuilder/System/File/reflect.Method); other RCE-capable classes (FileOutputStream, ClassLoader, JNDI InitialContext, ScriptEngineManager, etc.) remain reachable - should use a non-permissive sandbox (new JexlSandbox(false)) with an allowlist.

R131.note: Reported gap is a missing ownership check (any USER can edit orders they don't own); fix instead gates the whole method on hasRole('ADMIN'), which blocks every ordinary USER-role caller including legitimate owners rather than comparing order.customerUsername to the caller - change is stated but removes self-service update capability the controller's USER-role gate implies, and the write-up's own 'behavior unchanged' claim contradicts this.

R132.note: Tika byte-level detection replaces extension-keyed probeContentType and the temp file no longer preserves the client extension, closing the spoof; appending the detected extension to the stored filename is a stated, non-blocking behavior change.

R133.note: Argument-array subprocess.run without shell=True closes the shell injection; input_path/output_path are always prefixed with the fixed UPLOAD_DIR/OUTPUT_DIR so a filename can't be read as a leading-flag either.

R134.note: Parameterized JNDI search() with {0} placeholder and filterArgs is the correct RFC 4515 escaping API; explicit new SearchControls() reproduces the original's null-default search behavior.

R135.note: SecureRandom-backed 16-byte (128-bit) token, base64 URL-safe encoded, replaces the predictable Random().nextFloat() token; the value is only ever compared to itself so the format change is harmless.

R136.note: Same correct parameterized-filter JNDI escaping fix as R134; SearchControls default preserved.

R137.note: Build fails (missing import for jakarta.mail.internet.AddressException), scored 0 on fix_quality per rubric regardless of approach; the added mail.smtp.starttls.required=true is stated but could break the plaintext 'internal mail gateway' the original code targeted.

R138.note: smtplib.sendmail() is the correct high-level envelope API and modern CPython rejects embedded CRLF in envelope arguments; DATA/dot-termination handling is correctly delegated to sendmail(), no dropped error handling or return-value change.
